messages:
alex: Quick question — RFC said we can swap GQA/MQA kernels at runtime via the selector. Are we committed to strict ABI/backcompat for the KV cache layout or can we have a migration path?

mira: We penciled a "soft-compat" idea in the RFC but didn't nail it. My instinct: require a handshake that advertises a `kernel_schema_version` and a stable `cookie` for cached prefixes.

dan: +1. Handshake should be cheap. If versions mismatch, we should avoid cross-kernel reads and either invalidate or fall back.

sandeep: For Dedicated customers we need a zero-downtime plan. Can we support dual-mode (both old/new caches) for a short window during rollout? what's perf hit?

jen: Dual-mode is feasible but memory overhead isn't free. Expect ~5-10% RAM bump for duplicate KV entries. Also increases eviction churn.

alex: What about encoding a tiny version header on requests so we don't accidentally route a request expecting new layout to an old kernel? e.g. `X-Kernel-Version: 3` in transport.

mira: That works. Proposal sketch for handshake (pseudo):
```json
{"kernel_schema_version": 3, "supports_dual_cache": true, "cookie": "sha1:abcd..."}
```
If handshake fails, kernel returns `HANDSHAKE_MISMATCH` and selector triggers fallback policy.

infra-bot: Selector policy updated: `on_handshake_mismatch => route_to_fallback_kernel` (config change applied to staging).

dan: Fallback should default to single-query kernel (MQA) if integrity can't be guaranteed. Slower, but safe. Also emit a `kernel.handshake.mismatch` metric with sample count.

sandeep: Telemetry + alerting: add `kernel.handshake.duration`, `kernel.handshake.status` and `kv.eviction_on_mismatch` so we can track rollout regressions.

jen: Edge-case: streaming responses where client holds a continuation token and we flip kernels mid-stream. We need to invalidate or translate tokens on mismatch or force stream restart.

alex: Good call. Also need to document migration steps for Dedicated customers: 1) enable `supports_dual_cache` on new hosts, 2) start routing 10% of traffic, 3) monitor handshake metrics, 4) ramp and finally cutover.

mira: I'll draft a short follow-up RFC with the handshake contract, eviction rules, and compatibility matrix. Will include unit+integration tests in runtime test harness.

dan: I'll own the telemetry plumbing and a quick lint rule to forbid silent cache schema changes.

sandeep: I'll run a perf sweep to quantify memory/perf delta for dual-mode at 1k and 10k concurrent sessions.

alex: Thanks all. I'll open the RFC draft and mention owners. @mira @dan @sandeep please thumbs up when you have time.

infra-bot: New RFC branch created: `rfc/mqa-gqa-handshake-compat` — link: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/723 :thumbsup:

jen: acked, will add stream-token tests.

alex: Filing a small follow-up issue to track Dedicated migration checklist.

mira: Sounds good. small note: let's also consider a "rollforward" mode where old kernels accept new keys but ignore unknown flags to reduce churn. Will add to draft. :+1:
